key_insight: Stacked LCUs introduce a single control knob—the number of layers—that tunes the trade-off between trainability and classical simulability.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum algorithm designers a practical way to choose ansätze that are more trainable without losing all computational hardness.
method: Propose a stacked linear combination of unitaries (S-LCU) variational ansatz.
Analyze the Free Fermion S-LCU using diagrammatic methods.
Derive variance and complexity bounds that scale with the layer count l.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a variance lower bound of Ω(1/(n k^{3l})) and compares classical simulation cost O(k^{2l} n^3) against quantum gate complexity O(lkn^2).
watch_item: Increasing the number of layers improves expressivity but also raises both quantum circuit depth and classical simulation cost, so hardware limits and scaling must be checked carefully.
paper_title: Stacking the Deck: Tunable Trainability in Stacked LCUs
